text: DonSeTch 是 DeepSeek Harness 的网页检索与抓取插件，通过注册 MCP 工具并接入原生 web_search，让 agent 可以搜索网页、抓取单页内容、爬取整个站点并查看服务状态。插件监督本机 DonSeTch 服务进程，支持配置变更后重启服务，并可检查和切换已验证的程序版本。它适合需要在 DSH 会话中查找资料、读取网页或收集站点内容的用户；安装后可使用默认配置，搜索引擎密钥按需由 DonSeTch 配置。

DonSeTch adds web search, page fetching, and site crawling to DeepSeek Harness through MCP tools and its native web_search provider. It supervises a local service and supports verified updates. DSH users can start with defaults and add provider credentials when needed.

怎么让 DSH 自带的 web_search 使用 DonSeTch 搜索服务？
希望网页工具出错时能查看服务状态和诊断信息。
想在不手动配置 MCP 的情况下把网页能力接进 DSH。
How can I search the web from a DeepSeek Harness session?
I need my DSH agent to fetch pages and crawl a website.
DonSeTch 的网页搜索：通过注册的搜索 provider 调用 web_search，可传入查询词和可选结果数，并将结果映射回 Harness。
DonSeTch 的网页抓取与爬取：注册 MCP 服务公布的 fetch 和 crawl 工具，代理参数与结果，并将调用展示为 DSH 工具卡片。
DonSeTch 的状态诊断：调用 donsetch_status 可查看服务状态、已注册工具、程序版本、配置与密钥文件位置，以及 donsetch doctor 输出。

@dsh-external/donsetch README · donsetch-dsh：First-class DonSeTch web access for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (`dsh`). One install line, and every dsh agent gets the full DonSeTch suite: fetch, search, and crawl with browser-grade stealth, keyless engines, BYOK providers, and an auto-updating native binary. No API key required to start.

@dsh-external/donsetch README · Install：```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add github:dondai44423/donsetch-dsh
```

Restart `dsh web` (bundle plugins activate on the next boot). On first start the plugin downloads the correct DonSeTch binary for your platform from GitHub Releases, verifies its SHA256 against the release sidecar, and registers the tools. That is the whole setup: no API key, no config file.

Add the `dsh-plugin` topic to your repo mentions: this repo is already on it. The plugin also works in headless profiles:

@dsh-external/donsetch README · What you get：- `donsetch_web_fetch`: one URL to full markdown, browser-grade rendering and stealth where needed
- `donsetch_web_search`: keyless engines out of the box, or your own keys via BYOK providers (Exa, Tavily, Serper, SerpApi, SerpBase, Bright Data, TinyFish, plus plugin adapters)
- `donsetch_web_crawl`: whole-site crawling with sitemap discovery
- `donsetch_status`: self-diagnostics (degraded daemons get one automatically)
- Native `web_search`: the harness's own web_search tool routes through DonSeTch (the bundle patch selects the `donsetch` search provider), so ordinary searches work with no DeepSeek API key

@dsh-external/donsetch README · What you get：The tools are registered in-process on the harness tool registry, not as `mcp__*` imports, so they flow through dsh's permission, timeout, and cancellation pipeline like any native tool, and they show call/result cards in the Web workbench.
@dsh-external/donsetch README · Why it is not just an MCP config：dsh ships a built-in MCP client. Pointing it at `donsetch mcp` works, but this plugin is the first-class version:
section: Why it is not just an MCP config

text:
@dsh-external/donsetch README · Why it is not just an MCP config：| | built-in MCP config | this plugin |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Install | you write a config row | one plugin add |
| Binary download + SHA256 verify | manual install | automatic |
| Auto-updates with donsetch releases | never | yes, throttled, swappable between calls |
| Tool names | `mcp__donsetch__...` | `donsetch_...` |
| Config changes from the CLI | restart everything | live daemon restart on config file change |
| Workbench cards | generic | per-tool call/result summaries |
| Status + doctor for the agent | none | `donsetch_status` |
| Harness schema contract | none | parameters comply with the enforced raw JSON Schema contract |
| Correctness gate in CI | none | the plugin runs inside a real dsh ToolRuntime on every push |

@dsh-external/donsetch README · How customization works：The plugin uses the exact same config file the standard DonSeTch CLI uses, so every part of DonSeTch's normal customization applies unchanged:

```bash
donsetch keys add exa <key>         # add a provider key
donsetch keys default exa           # switch default provider
donsetch doctor                     # engine diagnostics
donsetch mcp ...                    # identical surface elsewhere
@dsh-external/donsetch README · How customization works：CLI changes land in the live dsh plugin within seconds: the plugin watches the config file and swaps the daemon without a dsh restart.

@dsh-external/donsetch README · Configuration：All defaults are sensible; the plugin works with zero configuration. Options come from the bundle patch (edit `$DSH_HOME/cordis.patch.yml` to override) plus environment variables.

@dsh-external/donsetch README · Configuration：| option | default | description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `toolPrefix` | `donsetch` | Model-facing tool name prefix, `[A-Za-z0-9_]{1,16}` |
| `channel` | `stable` | Update channel: `stable` (releases) or `latest` (includes prereleases) |
| `autoUpdate` | `true` | Check GitHub Releases and swap in newer verified binaries between calls |
| `updateIntervalHours` | `24` | Minimum gap between update checks |
| `callTimeoutMs` | `180000` | Per-tool-call timeout |
| `bootTimeoutMs` | `20000` | Daemon initialize + tools/list timeout |
| `fallbackToPath` | `true` | Use a `donsetch` already on PATH when the download fails (degraded mode, told honestly in `donsetch_status`) |
| `pinnedVersion` | current | donsetch release a fresh install pins (floor, not ceiling) |

@dsh-external/donsetch README · Configuration：Environment: `DONSETCH_DSH_PREFIX`, `DONSETCH_DSH_CHANNEL`, `DONSETCH_DSH_AUTOUPDATE=off`, `DONSETCH_BIN` (path to a local donsetch binary), `DONSETCH_DSH_CACHE_DIR`.

Patch-layer example (`$DSH_HOME/cordis.patch.yml`, later layers win):

```yaml
- override:
    - id: donsetch
      config:
        toolPrefix: web

@dsh-external/donsetch README · Updates：Two-layer update story. The plugin glue is a bundle: re-running `dsh plugin add` against a newer pin (or letting the repository panel track the branch) keeps it current. The donsetch binary updates itself: on a throttled schedule it checks GitHub Releases on your channel, and when a newer release appears it downloads, SHA256-verifies against the release sidecar, and swaps the daemon between in-flight calls. A failed verify aborts the install and keeps the current binary; nothing partial ever replaces a working daemon.
@dsh-external/donsetch README · Updates：The baseline DonSeTch pin auto-tracks published releases every 6 hours.

@dsh-external/donsetch README · Reliability notes：- The daemon runs supervised (`donsetch mcp --supervised`), so crashes restart transparently and the next tool call revives cleanly.
- Cancellations reach the real daemon (`notifications/cancelled`), the in-flight fetch or crawl actually stops.
- Plugin unload kills the daemon: hot-reload leaves no orphan processes.
- Downloads are atomic: temp dir, hash check, rename into place, stale dirs removed.
- The update check never blocks tool service and never runs a paid query.
- A `url` that is a string beginning with `[` (a batch array serialized into one scalar) is rejected before the daemon with an error that names the shape and the fix, instead of the binary's `url must be http(s)`, which never mentions arrays. It is rejected, not coerced: the schema has one encoding for one URL and one for a batch, and silently accepting a third hides the mistake from the caller.

@dsh-external/donsetch README · Compatibility：Developer preview caveat: DeepSeek Harness is iterating fast and its APIs are moving. This plugin pins no host-train imports at all (it talks to the harness only through the `ctx` handed to `apply()`), which keeps it installable across harness updates. Verified against:

@dsh-external/donsetch README · Compatibility：| harness | npm dsh | dsh-tools |
| --- | --- | --- |
| DeepSeek Harness 0.1.1-rc.2 (npm latest) | `@deepseek-ai/dsh` | 0.1.x train |
| DeepSeek Harness 0.1.2-alpha.1 (source docs) | source | 0.1.x train |
| DeepSeek Harness 0.2.1-rc.5 (packed-plugin install and profile composition) | `@deepseek-ai/dsh` | registry tests remain on the 0.1.x train |

Node `^22.19.0 || >=24.0.0` (the harness requirement).

@dsh-external/donsetch README · Compatibility：The fresh-install smoke uses dsh 0.2.1-rc.5 and pnpm 10.20.0 on Windows. Profile composition also works locally on Linux with that host; the older Linux pty-prebuild limitation does not apply to this composition check. Install pnpm on PATH before using `dsh plugin add`; dsh does not bundle it.

@dsh-external/donsetch README · Troubleshooting：**Tools are missing in a session.** Ask the agent to call `donsetch_status`, or check the plugin log lines (`[donsetch] ...`) on the dsh host. The status tool reports the daemon state, binary version, last boot error, and the `donsetch doctor` output.

**First install failed.** Offline? The plugin falls back to a `donsetch` on PATH (degraded, told honestly). To pin a local binary instead, set `DONSETCH_BIN=/path/to/donsetch`.

@dsh-external/donsetch README · Troubleshooting：**I want the old-version binary.** Delete the versioned dir under `~/.cache/donsetch/dsh/bin/` and the plugin reinstalls the pinned release.

**A call says "url looks like a stringified array".** The caller meant a batch and sent `"[A, B]"`, one string. A batch is a real JSON array (`["A", "B"]`); anything else is one http(s) URL or handle per call. The guard rejects before the daemon, so nothing was fetched.

@dsh-external/donsetch README · Development：```bash
npm install
npm test        # typecheck + build + unit/integration suite (fake daemon harness)
npm run live    # real donsetch binary: handshake + tools/list + fetch + search
npm run lint    # house style (no em-dashes in shipped text)

`dist/` is committed on purpose: git installs then skip build scripts entirely and dsh users never see the pnpm 10 `allowBuilds` prompt.
@dsh-external/donsetch README · Development：The repo is structured like donsetch itself: `project.md` + `status.md` are private working docs, gitignored, updated after every finished task.
